announced.quote: 9 July 2018 | By ATLAS Collaboration ... Today, at the 2018 International Conference on High Energy Physics (ICHEP) in Seoul, the ATLAS experiment reported a preliminary result establishing the observation of the Higgs boson decaying into pairs of b quarks

claim.quote: which yields an observed (expected) significance of 5.4 (5.5) standard deviations, thus providing direct observation of the Higgs boson decay into b-quarks.

date.note: Announcement date: ATLAS reported a preliminary result establishing the observation at ICHEP 2018 (Seoul) on 9 July 2018. The final paper was submitted to arXiv on 24 August 2018 and published as Phys. Lett. B 786 (2018) 59.
date.quote: 9 July 2018 | By ATLAS Collaboration ... Today, at the 2018 International Conference on High Energy Physics (ICHEP) in Seoul, the ATLAS experiment reported a preliminary result establishing the observation of the Higgs boson decaying into pairs of b quarks

name: Observation of the Higgs boson decay to bottom quarks

significance.quote: an observed (expected) significance of 5.4 (5.5) standard deviations
significance.value: 5.4σ observed (5.5σ expected), combination of Run 1 and Run 2 H → bb̄ searches

summary.plain: ATLAS reports the observation of the Higgs boson decaying into bottom quarks, which the paper describes as the Standard Model Higgs boson's dominant decay (expected branching fraction about 58%). The main search looked for it produced together with a W or Z boson.
summary.technical: Search for H → bb̄ produced with a W or Z boson (VH) in 79.8 fb^-1 of 13 TeV data: observed (expected) significance 4.9 (4.3) standard deviations; combined with Run 1 and other Run 2 H → bb̄ searches: 5.4 (5.5) standard deviations, 'direct observation of the Higgs boson decay into b-quarks'. Ratio of the measured H → bb̄ yield to the Standard Model expectation 1.01 ± 0.12 (stat) +0.16/−0.15 (syst); VH production observed at 5.3 (4.8) standard deviations (Run 2 combination).

title: Observation of H -> bbbar decays and VH production with the ATLAS detector
why_it_matters: H → bb̄ is the dominant decay of the Standard Model Higgs boson, but large multijet backgrounds make a search in the dominant gluon–gluon fusion production mode difficult, so the search uses production with a W or Z boson. The ratio of the measured H → bb̄ yield to the Standard Model expectation is 1.01 ± 0.12 (stat) +0.16/−0.15 (syst).
